See [§ Node ownership](#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node) and [connector/impl.md — No-Live-Tenant / Planned Configuration](references/plugins/connector/impl.md#no-live-tenant--planned-configuration).

128	- **Never route an `error` port back into the happy path** — an error edge into the next happy-path node, or into the same End node the success path reaches, makes every failed run report `Completed` with success-shaped outputs. 131	- **Never hand-write `definitions` entries** — always copy from registry output. Hand-written definitions have wrong port schemas and cause validation failures.
132	- **Never put any `model` block on node instances** — BPMN type, serviceType, event definition, binding templates, and context templates all live in the node's **definition** (copied verbatim from `registry get` into `definitions[]`). 33	## Three-turn execution map
34	
35	Steps 0–6 are **logical phases**, not separate turns. A typical greenfield build collapses to **three assistant turns** (universal SKILL.md rule #10). Each step heading below carries a `[T1]` / `[T2]` / `[T3]` tag — emit every tool call inside the same Turn as one assistant message.
36	
37	| Turn | Steps | What you emit in ONE assistant message |
38	|---|---|---|
39	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-execution-map-intro:end-->
40	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:start-->
41	| **T1 — Setup + discovery** | 0, 1, 2, 3 | One chained `Bash` (scaffold + register + pull + `node add` for each CLI-owned node) **+** parallel `Bash` (one `registry get` per OOTB type you'll inline) **+** parallel `Read` (plugin `impl.md`s). **If existing `.uipx` solutions are present, the Step 2 gate fires first in its own turn** — resolve it before this chain. |
42	| **T2 — Read + author** | 4 | One `Read` of the `.flow` **+** a batch of `Edit` calls (or one `Write` if ≥70% of nodes change). Claude Code serializes Edits on the same file, so they don't race |
43	| **T3 — Finalize** | 5, 6 | One chained `Bash` (`node configure && validate && format`). On validate failure: one Edit turn, then re-chain `validate && format` |
44	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t1-execution:end-->

46	### Batching anti-patterns
47	
48	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:start-->
49	- **One CLI per turn.** Never issue `solution init`, then `cd`, then `flow init` as three separate Bash calls — chain with `&&`, the `cd` included as its own segment. Same for `node configure && validate && format`.
50	- **Sequential `registry get`s.** Emit every `registry get` as a parallel `Bash` in one message alongside the T1 scaffold chain.
51	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-init-batching:end-->
52	- **Validating after every Edit.** Validate once at the end of T3 (or after a recovery Edit). Intermediate states are expected to be invalid.
53	- **Re-reading the `.flow` every turn.** `Read` once at the start of T2; subsequent `Edit`s in the same conversation don't need re-reading unless an external command (e.g., `node configure`, `format`) rewrites the file between Edits.
54	- **`Edit` in the same turn as a `Bash` that mutates the same file.** Parallel tool calls race — separate them across turns.
55	- **Two parallel `Edit`s anchored to the same byte range.** Same-file Edits serialize in execution order; if Edit N's `old_string` overlaps text that Edit N-1's substitution removed or shifted, Edit N fails with "string not found." Use the [per-array anchor pattern](#anchoring-parallel-flow-edits--anchor-on-what-you-read-not-on-key-order) — anchor each Edit on its target array's own opening key, never on key order or a shared boundary.

85	## Step 2 — Create a solution, THEN a Flow project inside it **[T1]**
86	
87	> **A Flow project cannot exist outside a solution** (universal rule in [SKILL.md](../../../SKILL.md)). Run `uip maestro flow init` (Step 2b) outside a solution and it now **auto-scaffolds** one — `<Project>Solution/<Project>Solution.uipx` with the project nested at `<Project>Solution/<Project>/` (response carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution`). 94	### Canonical T1 chain — issue this as ONE `Bash` call
95	
96	This is the consolidated command that does Steps 2a + 2b + Step 3 + (optionally) one `node add` per CLI-owned node, in one chained Bash. `node add` signature is `<file> <node-type>` (file first):
97	
98	```bash
99	uip solution init "<SolutionName>" --output json \
100	  && cd "<SolutionName>" \
101	  && uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>" --output json \
102	  && cd "<ProjectName>" \
103	  && uip maestro flow registry pull \
104	  && uip maestro flow node add "<ProjectName>.flow" core.action.http.v2 --label "<NodeLabel>" --output json
105	```
106	
107	> **One creation path — never drop the `cd`.** `uip solution init "<SolutionName>"` → `cd "<SolutionName>"` → `uip maestro flow init "<ProjectName>"`, one chain. Without the `cd`, `flow init` runs in the old directory and auto-scaffolds a duplicate `<ProjectName>Solution/` (1-node husk). Never let auto-scaffold create the solution. Finish with exactly one `project.uiproj` — delete strays.
108	
109	Tail-append one `node add` per CLI-owned node (`uipath.connector.*`, `uipath.connector.trigger.*`, `core.action.http.v2`). Each `node add` returns the new node `id` in `Data` — capture it from the chained output for T2/T3. Drop the trailing `node add` segment when the flow is OOTB-only.

111	In the SAME assistant message (parallel to this chain): emit one `Bash` per OOTB `registry get <NODE_TYPE>` you'll need in T2 (always `core.control.end` — see Step 4), and parallel `Read` calls for any plugin `impl.md`s you'll consult.

113	> **Older `solution-tool` (< 1.0.0)** used `solution new` (see [.claude/rules/cli-renames.md](../../../../../.claude/rules/cli-renames.md)). If `solution init` returns `unknown command`, substitute `solution new`.

117	### 2a. Create a new solution
118

123	Creates `<cwd>/<SolutionName>/<SolutionName>.uipx`. **`cd` into the new solution directory before Step 2b.**

125	> **Naming convention:** In **pure greenfield** (no existing solutions), default the solution name to the project name unless the user specifies otherwise. 129	```bash
130	cd <directory>/<SolutionName> && uip maestro flow init <ProjectName> --output json
131	```

133	The `cd` puts the project inside the solution you just created. Skip it and `flow init` won't find that solution (discovery walks **up**, not down into `<SolutionName>/`) — it auto-scaffolds a **second, separate** `<ProjectName>Solution/` beside your empty `<SolutionName>/`, leaving two solutions. The project no longer single-nests, but `cd` first to land in the right one.
134	
135	> **Bash session state persists across tool calls.** This `cd` is **not scoped to one Bash invocation** — your cwd remains inside `<SolutionName>/` for every subsequent `Bash` call until you `cd` somewhere else. 137	`--output json` is required so Step 2c can inspect `Data.SolutionRegistration.Status` to confirm the project was auto-registered with the parent solution.

139	### 2c. Verify the project is registered in the solution
140	
141	When `uip maestro flow init` is run from inside a solution directory (Step 2b), it **auto-registers** the project with the nearest parent `.uipx`. Run outside any solution, it **auto-scaffolds** `<Project>Solution/` and registers the project in it — the response then also carries `Data.AutoCreatedSolution` (`{ Name, Path, SolutionFile }`) and `Status: Registered`. Pass `--skip-solution-registration` to opt out of both (Status `OptedOut`, bare single-nested layout). The success envelope always reports the outcome in `Data.SolutionRegistration`:

143	```json
144	{
145	  "Result": "Success",
146	  "Code": "FlowInit",
147	  "Data": {
148	    "Status": "Created successfully",
149	    "Path": ".../<SolutionName>/<ProjectName>",
150	    "SolutionRegistration": {
151	      "Status": "Registered",                     // or "AlreadyRegistered"
152	      "Solution": ".../<SolutionName>.uipx",
153	      "Project": "<ProjectName>/project.uiproj",
154	      "ProjectId": "<uuid>"
155	    }
156	  }
157	}
158	```

162	**Fallback** — when `Status` is `Skipped` (ambiguous discovery — e.g. multiple `.uipx`), `Failed` (the `.uipx` write failed), or `NotInSolution` (rare — auto-scaffold did not run and no parent `.uipx` was found): wire the project manually.

261	
262	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-build-scaffold-assumptions:start-->
263	> **`flow init` scaffolds ONLY the manual trigger (`start` / `core.trigger.manual`) with zero edges.** Every other user-owned node — **including the End node** — is yours to add via `Edit` / `Write`. 266	### T2 batch — issue these in ONE assistant message
267	
268	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:start-->
269	1. **One `Read`** of `<ProjectName>.flow` — required before any Edit/Write; T1's chained Bash mutated the file and Claude Code's file-state tracker does not auto-refresh on external mutations.
270	<!--skill-flavor:greenfield-t2-read-source:end-->
271	2. **A batch of parallel `Edit` calls** — one per top-level array you're modifying. Same-file Edits serialize in execution order, so each `old_string` must anchor to text NO OTHER parallel Edit modifies. Use the **per-array anchor pattern** below.
272	   - Edit `nodes[]` — add the End node (and any other user-owned nodes).
273	   - Edit `definitions[]` — paste the End definition verbatim from T1's `registry get core.control.end` output.
274	   - Edit `edges[]` — wire `trigger → <httpNode> → end`. End-node `outputs` mapping goes here too if you declared an `out` variable in `variables.globals`.
275	   - Edit `layout.nodes` — placeholder `{ position: { x: 0, y: 0 }, size: { width: 96, height: 96 }, collapsed: false }` per new node; `format` rewrites both position and size (by node shape) in T3.
276	
277	   `Write` of the whole file is allowed but token-costly on flows >~10 nodes — only fall back to `Write` when ≥70% of nodes change AND the file is small (see [editing-operations.md — Tool Selection Ladder](editing-operations.md#tool-selection-ladder)). **Never `Write` a flow that already has connector / connector-trigger / managed-HTTP nodes** — the rewrite clobbers their CLI-owned `bindings[]` / `inputs.detail` (invisible to `flow validate`); `Edit` in place, or re-run `node configure` as the last write. See [CAPABILITY.md — Node ownership](../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node).
278	
279	#### Anchoring parallel `.flow` Edits — anchor on what you Read, not on key order
280	
281	> **Do not assume a top-level key order.** The CLI does not guarantee which keys are present or in what sequence — fixtures show `runtime` before `nodes` on one flow and absent on another, and `bindings` / `variables` / `solutionId` / `projectId` / `metadata` appear in varying positions. Any anchor of the form "closing `]` + the NEXT top-level key" is coupled to that ordering and will silently break across CLI versions or between flows. **Anchor on the target array's OWN key instead — you just `Read` the file at the top of T2, so anchor to text that read actually contains.**
282	
283	Anchor each Edit using its target array's own opening key, located in the text you just Read — not adjacency to a neighbor key. The catch: `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT unique in the file. They recur **inside inline `definitions[]`** (an HTTP v2 / agent / subprocess definition embeds its own nested `nodes`/`edges`) **and inside any `subflows.<id>` block** (each subflow holds its own `nodes`/`edges`) — so even a small flow can carry several copies. The reliable, version-independent discriminator is **indentation: the top-level array sits at 2-space indent; every nested one is deeper.** `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` appear once each, so they need no disambiguation.
284	
285	| Edit target | Anchor on (from the text you Read) | How to insert |
286	|---|---|---|
287	| Append to `nodes[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "nodes": [` (the top-level array — deeper-indented `"nodes": ["` inside definitions do not match the two-leading-space prefix) plus the `start` node's opening `{ "id": "start"`. | Insert the new node object as the first element, immediately after the `[`: `\n    { new node JSON },`. Head-insertion keeps `old_string` clear of the array's closing `]`. |
288	| Append to `edges[]` | The **2-space-indented** `\n  "edges": [`. A newly generated scaffold commonly has `\n  "edges": []`; the 2-space prefix distinguishes it from nested `edges` arrays. | When empty, replace `\n  "edges": []` with `\n  "edges": [\n    { new edge JSON }\n  ]`. When non-empty, anchor through the first edge and insert the new edge as the first element. |
289	| Append to `definitions[]` | `"definitions": [` plus the first definition's opening bytes. Top-level `definitions[]` is the only one in the file, so this is reliably unique. | Insert the new definition right after the opening `[`, as the first element. Never anchor on whatever key follows `definitions` — that key varies (`runtime`, `bindings`, `variables`, `layout`, depending on CLI version and what the flow contains). |
290	| Add an entry to `layout.nodes` | `"layout": {\n    "nodes": {\n      "start":` — `start` is the always-present trigger and the first key under `layout.nodes` in newly generated flows. The top-level `"layout": {` is the only one. | `"layout":` + `"start":` jointly disambiguate. Insert `"<newId>": { ... },\n      ` before `"start":`. CLI-owned nodes added via `node add` already have a `layout.nodes` entry — only add entries for nodes you author by hand (e.g. End). |
291	
292	**Why head-insertion.** Inserting the new element right after the array's opening `[` means the `old_string` never includes the array's closing `]` — so it cannot collide with a closing `]` from a nested object (`form.sections[].fields[]`), and it never references a sibling top-level key whose position is not guaranteed. JSON array element order is not semantically significant for `nodes` / `edges` / `definitions`, so head vs. tail insertion is equivalent; `flow format` normalizes layout regardless.
293	
294	**Disjointness rule.** Two parallel Edits MUST anchor on DIFFERENT top-level arrays — nodes-Edit on the top-level `nodes[]`, edges-Edit on the top-level `edges[]`, definitions-Edit on `definitions[]`, layout-Edit on `layout.nodes`. Because each anchors on its own array (not a shared boundary), the parallel Edits never overlap — provided each anchor is unique first (see below).
295	
296	**Pre-flight uniqueness check.** Before submitting an Edit, confirm your `old_string` appears **exactly once** in the file you Read. `"definitions": [` and the top-level `"layout": {` are reliably unique. `"nodes": [` and `"edges": [` are NOT — they recur inside inline definitions and subflows, so anchor on the **2-space-indented** occurrence and extend through the first element's opening (e.g. `"id": "start"`) until the match count is one. Never anchor on a bare bracket shape, and never assume the first textual occurrence is the top-level one.
297	
298	**Safer fallback when in doubt:** serialize the Edits across two turns. One extra turn is cheaper than a failed-Edit recovery loop (which forces a re-Read, a re-derived anchor, and a re-submit).
299	
300	See [shared/file-format.md — Top-level structure](../../shared/file-format.md#top-level-structure) for which top-level keys exist and the note that their order is not guaranteed.
301	
302	> **Intra-turn ordering.** If a parallel `Edit` fails with "file not read," split `Read` into its own turn (cost: +1 turn).

321	
322	```bash

324	  && uip maestro flow validate "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json \
325	  && uip maestro flow format "<ProjectName>.flow" --output json
326	```
327	
328	`<DETAIL_JSON>` is node-type-specific — the schema is owned by each CLI-owned node's plugin, not duplicated here: HTTP → [http/impl.md](plugins/http/impl.md#critical-use-node-configure), connectors → [connector/impl.md](plugins/connector/impl.md), connector triggers → [connector-trigger/impl.md](plugins/connector-trigger/impl.md). 330	> **The plugin `impl.md` is authoritative — follow its full procedure, not just its `--detail` schema, and let it override this turn map.** A plugin may prescribe steps the three-turn collapse does not show — most importantly a **pre-`configure` live fetch** whose output you must read before you can author `--detail` (the value depends on the live response, so it cannot be guessed or copied from a doc example). When `impl.md` defines such a step, run it in its **own turn before T3** and build `--detail` from its result; do not batch it into the chain, skip it, or hand-author the payload. 2	
3	## Node Type
4	
5	`core.logic.loop`
6	
7	## Registry Validation
8	
9	```bash
10	uip maestro flow registry get core.logic.loop --output json
11	```
12	
13	Confirm: input ports `input` and `loopBack`, output ports `success` and `output`, required input `collection`. Set the node instance `typeVersion` to the `version` field from this response — do not hardcode it.
14	
15	## JSON Structure
16	
17	### Loop node
18	
19	```json
20	{
21	  "id": "loop1",
22	  "type": "core.logic.loop",
23	  "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
24	  "display": { "label": "Loop over items" },
25	  "inputs": {
26	    "collection": "=js:$vars.fetchData.output.body.items",
27	    "parallel": false
28	  }
29	}
30	```
31	
32	> **Collection source shape depends on the node type.** Connector `list` activities return the bare array — `"collection": "=js:$vars.searchIssuesByJql1.output"`, NOT `.output.issues` / `.output.items`. HTTP nodes differ — envelope preserved: `.output.body.<key>` as above. See [connector/impl.md — Connector output shape](../connector/impl.md).
33	
34	Set `"parallel": true` to execute all iterations concurrently.
35	
36	### Loop body nodes — `parentId` required
37	
38	Every node inside the loop body **must** have `"parentId"` set to the loop node's ID. Without this, the runtime does not know the node is part of the loop and variableUpdates will not fire per-iteration.
39	
40	```json
41	{
42	  "id": "processItem",
43	  "type": "core.action.script",
44	  "typeVersion": "1.0",
45	  "display": { "label": "Process item" },
46	  "inputs": {
47	    "script": "return $vars.product * $vars.loop1.currentItem"
48	  },
49	  "parentId": "loop1"
50	}
51	```
52	
53	> **Critical:** If you omit `parentId`, the node executes outside the loop context. State variables will not update across iterations and loop outputs like `currentItem` will be inaccessible.
54	
55	## Adding / Editing
56	
57	For step-by-step add, delete, and wiring procedures, see [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md). Use the JSON structure above for the node-specific `inputs` and `parentId`.
58	
59	### CLI carve-out nodes inside a loop
60	
61	When adding a CLI carve-out node (connector, connector trigger, or managed HTTP) inside a loop, pass `--parent` to set `parentId` automatically:
62	
63	```bash
64	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> core.action.http.v2 --label "Fetch data" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
65	uip maestro flow node add <FLOW_PATH> <CONNECTOR_NODE_TYPE> --label "Get record" --parent <LOOP_ID> --output json
66	```
67	
68	`--parent` validates the parent node exists and sets `parentId` on the new node. For non-carve-out node types (script, end, etc.), set `"parentId"` directly in the JSON — see the examples above.

70	## Wiring
71	
72	Loop nodes have a specific wiring pattern:
73	
74	- `input` — entry from upstream
75	- `output` — into the loop body (first body node)
76	- `loopBack` — return from last body node back to loop
77	- `success` — exit after loop completes (to next downstream node)
78	
79	See [editing-operations.md](../../editing-operations.md) for edge add procedures.

81	## Accessing Loop Variables Inside Body
82	
83	Inside the loop body, access the current item via `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`:
84	
85	```javascript
86	// In a Script node inside the loop body (parentId must be set to the loop node)
87	const item = $vars.loop1.currentItem;
88	const index = $vars.loop1.currentIndex;
89	return { processed: item.name.toUpperCase(), position: index };
90	```
91	
92	| Variable | Description |
93	| --- | --- |
94	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | The item being processed in this iteration |
95	| `$vars.<loopId>.currentIndex` | 0-based iteration index |
96	| `$vars.<loopId>.collection` | The full collection being iterated |
97	
98	> **Do not use `iterator.currentItem`.** The correct access pattern is `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` where `<loopId>` is the loop node's `id` (e.g., `$vars.loop1.currentItem`).
99	
100	### Required node variables for loop outputs
101	
102	For `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` etc. to resolve, you must add corresponding entries to `variables.nodes`:
103	
104	```json
105	{
106	  "variables": {
107	    "nodes": [
108	      {
109	        "id": "loop1.currentItem",
110	        "type": "any",
111	        "description": "The current item being iterated in the loop",
112	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" }
113	      },
114	      {
115	        "id": "loop1.currentIndex",
116	        "type": "number",
117	        "description": "The current iteration index (0-based)",
118	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" }
119	      },
120	      {
121	        "id": "loop1.collection",
122	        "type": "array",
123	        "description": "The collection being iterated over",
124	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" }
125	      },
126	      {
127	        "id": "loop1.output",
128	        "type": "array",
129	        "description": "Aggregated results from all loop iterations",
130	        "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" }
131	      }
132	    ]
133	  }
134	}
135	```

137	## State Accumulation with variableUpdates
138	
139	To accumulate state across loop iterations (counters, running totals), use an `inout` variable with a `variableUpdate` on the body node:
140	
141	```json
142	{
143	  "variables": {
144	    "globals": [
145	      {
146	        "id": "runningTotal",
147	        "direction": "inout",
148	        "type": "number",
149	        "defaultValue": 0
150	      }
151	    ],
152	    "variableUpdates": {
153	      "bodyNode": [
154	        {
155	          "variableId": "runningTotal",
156	          "expression": "=js:$vars.bodyNode.output"
157	        }
158	      ]
159	    }
160	  }
161	}
162	```
163	
164	The variableUpdate fires after each iteration, so the `inout` variable carries the accumulated value into the next iteration.
165	
166	> **Critical:** The variableUpdate expression **cannot** access loop iteration variables like `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem`. These are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). If you need to compute using `currentItem`, do the computation in the script and reference the script's output in the variableUpdate.
167

198	    },
199	    {
200	      "id": "end1",
201	      "type": "core.control.end",
202	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
203	      "display": { "label": "End" },
204	      "inputs": {},
205	      "outputs": {
206	        "result": { "source": "=js:$vars.accumulator" }
207	      }
208	    }
209	  ],
210	  "edges": [
211	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
212	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "bodyScript", "targetPort": "input" },
213	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "bodyScript", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "loopBack" },
214	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
215	  ],
216	  "variables": {
217	    "globals": [
218	      { "id": "inputItems", "direction": "in", "type": "array", "defaultValue": [] },
219	      { "id": "accumulator", "direction": "inout", "type": "number", "defaultValue": 0 },
220	      { "id": "result", "direction": "out", "type": "number" }
221	    ],
222	    "nodes": [
223	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
224	      { "id": "loop1.currentIndex", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIndex" } },

233	      ]
234	    }
235	  }
236	}
237	```

239	Key points in this pattern:
240	- `bodyScript` has `"parentId": "loop1"` — places it inside the loop
241	- Script accesses `$vars.loop1.currentItem` for the current iteration value
242	- `variableUpdate` on `bodyScript` writes the script's return value back to `accumulator`
243	- `accumulator` is `inout` so it persists across iterations
244	- End node maps the final accumulated value to the `out` variable
245	
246	## Complete Example — Multi-Node Loop Body (HTTP + Script)
247	
248	Loop over items, fetch data per-iteration via HTTP, process with a script. Both body nodes have `parentId`.
249	
250	```json
251	{
252	  "nodes": [
253	    {
254	      "id": "start",
255	      "type": "core.trigger.manual",
256	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
257	      "display": { "label": "Manual trigger" },
258	      "inputs": { "entryPointId": "..." }
259	    },
260	    {
261	      "id": "loop1",
262	      "type": "core.logic.loop",
263	      "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
264	      "display": { "label": "For each item" },
265	      "inputs": {
266	        "collection": "=js:[{ name: 'A', id: 1 }, { name: 'B', id: 2 }]",
267	        "parallel": false
268	      }
269	    },
270	    {
271	      "id": "fetchData1",
272	      "type": "core.action.http.v2",
273	      "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
274	      "display": { "label": "Fetch data" },
275	      "inputs": { "branches": [], "timeout": "PT15M", "retryCount": 0, "detail": {} },
276	      "parentId": "loop1"
277	    },
278	    {
279	      "id": "processItem1",
280	      "type": "core.action.script",
281	      "typeVersion": "<DEFINITION_VERSION>",
282	      "display": { "label": "Process item" },
283	      "inputs": {
284	        "script": "return { name: $vars.loop1.currentItem.name, value: $vars.fetchData1.output.body.result };"
285	      },
286	      "parentId": "loop1"
287	    },
288	    {
289	      "id": "end1",
290	      "type": "core.control.end",
291	      "typeVersion": "1.0",
292	      "display": { "label": "End" },
293	      "inputs": {},
294	      "outputs": { "results": { "source": "=js:$vars.loop1.output" } }
295	    }
296	  ],
297	  "edges": [
298	    { "id": "e1", "sourceNodeId": "start", "sourcePort": "output", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "input" },
299	    { "id": "e2", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "start", "targetNodeId": "fetchData1", "targetPort": "input" },
300	    { "id": "e3", "sourceNodeId": "fetchData1", "sourcePort": "default", "targetNodeId": "processItem1", "targetPort": "input" },
301	    { "id": "e4", "sourceNodeId": "processItem1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "loop1", "targetPort": "continue" },
302	    { "id": "e5", "sourceNodeId": "loop1", "sourcePort": "success", "targetNodeId": "end1", "targetPort": "input" }
303	  ],
304	  "variables": {
305	    "globals": [
306	      { "id": "results", "direction": "out", "type": "array" }
307	    ],
308	    "nodes": [
309	      { "id": "loop1.currentItem", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentItem" } },
310	      { "id": "loop1.currentIteration", "type": "number", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "currentIteration" } },
311	      { "id": "loop1.collection", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "collection" } },
312	      { "id": "loop1.output", "type": "array", "binding": { "nodeId": "loop1", "outputId": "output" } },
313	      { "id": "fetchData1.output", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchData1", "outputId": "output" } },
314	      { "id": "fetchData1.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "fetchData1", "outputId": "error" } },
315	      { "id": "processItem1.output", "type": "any", "binding": { "nodeId": "processItem1", "outputId": "output" } },
316	      { "id": "processItem1.error", "type": "object", "binding": { "nodeId": "processItem1", "outputId": "error" } }
317	    ]
318	  }
319	}
320	```
321	
322	- Both `fetchData1` and `processItem1` have `"parentId": "loop1"` — omitting it on either causes null outputs at runtime while validation passes
323	- HTTP body uses `start`/`default` ports; script returns via `success`/`continue`
324	- `detail` on HTTP node is abbreviated — populate via `uip maestro flow node configure`
325	
326	## Debug
327	
328	| Error | Cause | Fix |
329	| --- | --- | --- |
330	| Collection is empty or null | Expression evaluates to null/undefined | Check `collection` expression and upstream output |
331	| `$vars.loop1.currentItem` is undefined | Missing node variable binding or missing `parentId` | Add `loop1.currentItem` to `variables.nodes` and set `parentId` on body nodes |
332	| State variable not updating across iterations | Body node missing `parentId` | Add `"parentId": "<loopId>"` to every node inside the loop body |
333	| State variable becomes `NaN` | variableUpdate expression uses `$vars.<loopId>.currentItem` | Loop variables are not available in variableUpdate expressions. Do the computation in the script and reference `$vars.<bodyNodeId>.output` in the variableUpdate |
334	| Infinite loop | Edges wired incorrectly | Ensure only `loopBack` creates the cycle, not arbitrary edges |
335	| No output after loop | Missing `success` edge | Wire the `success` port to the next downstream node |

commands.result_summary: 1 # Variables and Expressions 2 3 Complete reference for declaring variables, writing expressions, and managing data flow in `.flow` files. 4 5 > **Read this before** adding variables or writing expressions in any flow. 6 > 7 > `flow validate` catches the structural expression-reference errors: 8 > 9 > - Missing `=js:` prefix on `$vars`/`$metadata`/`$self` (MST-9107) 10 > - Invented `nodes..output` syntax 11 > - References to unknown variables or node IDs 12 > - Output-path walks that descend into declared primitives or schemas closed with `additionalProperties: false` 13 > 14 > Errors against **open output schemas** (HTTP response bodies, script returns, free-text agent output) and **wrong-direction reads** (e.g. reading an `out`-only variable) still slip past validate and surface only at `flow debug` or in production. 15 16 --- 17 18 ## Table of contents 19 20 - [Variables Overview](#variables-overview) 21 - [Workflow Variables (`globals`)](#workflow-variables-globals) 22 - [Node Variables (`nodes`)](#node-variables-nodes) 23 - [Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`)](#variable-updates-variableupdates) 24 - [Output Mapping on End Nodes](#output-mapping-on-end-nodes) 25 - [Expression System](#expression-system) 26 - [Available Globals](#available-globals) 27 - [Expression Contexts](#expression-contexts) 28 - [Jint Engine Constraints](#jint-engine-constraints) 29 - [Scoping Rules](#scoping-rules) 30 - [Variable Management via CLI](#variable-management-via-cli) 31 - [Complete Example](#complete-example) 32 33 --- 34 35 ## Variables Overview 36 37 Every flow has a `variables` object at the top level of the `.flow` file. It contains three sections: 38 39 ```json 40 { 41 "variables": { 42 "globals": [], 43 "nodes": [], 44 "variableUpdates": {} 45 } 46 } 47 ``` 48 49 | Section | Purpose | 50 | --- | --- | 51 | `globals` | Workflow-level variables: inputs, outputs, and state | 52 | `nodes` | Node output variables (auto-generated when using CLI `node add`) | 53 | `variableUpdates` | Per-node expressions that update state variables | 54 55 --- 56 57 ## Workflow Variables (`globals`) 58 59 Workflow variables are declared in `variables.globals`. Each has a **direction** that determines its role. 60 61 ### Directions 62 63 | Direction | Role | Readable | Writable | Use case | 64 | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | 65 | `in` | External input | Yes | No | Values passed when the flow is triggered or called | 66 | `out` | Workflow output | Yes | Mapped on End node | Values returned when the flow completes | 67 | `inout` | Internal state | Yes | Yes (via `variableUpdates`) | Counters, accumulators, flags shared across nodes | 68 69 ### Schema 70 71 ```typescript 72 { 73 id: string // Unique identifier, used in expressions as $vars.{id} 74 direction: "in" | "out" | "inout" 75 type?: string // "string" (default), "number", "boolean", "object", "array", "file" 76 subType?: string // Item type for arrays (e.g., "object", "string") 77 schema?: object // JSON Schema (draft-07) for complex types 78 defaultValue?: unknown // Initial value (must match type) 79 description?: string // Human-readable description 80 triggerNodeId?: string // Trigger node this input is associated with (works in both root flows and subflows) 81 } 82 ``` 83 84 ### Examples 85 86 **String input with default:** 87 ```json 88 { 89 "id": "customerName", 90 "direction": "in", 91 "type": "string", 92 "defaultValue": "Unknown", 93 "description": "Name of the customer to process" 94 } 95 ``` 96 97 **Number output:** 98 ```json 99 { 100 "id": "totalAmount", 101 "direction": "out", 102 "type": "number" 103 } 104 ``` 105 106 **State variable (counter):** 107 ```json 108 { 109 "id": "retryCount", 110 "direction": "inout", 111 "type": "number", 112 "defaultValue": 0 113 } 114 ``` 115 116 **Object with JSON Schema:** 117 ```json 118 { 119 "id": "orderData", 120 "direction": "in", 121 "type": "object", 122 "schema": { 123 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 124 "type": "object", 125 "required": ["orderId", "amount"], 126 "properties": { 127 "orderId": { "type": "string" }, 128 "amount": { "type": "number" }, 129 "items": { 130 "type": "array", 131 "items": { "type": "object" } 132 } 133 }, 134 "additionalProperties": false 135 } 136 } 137 ``` 138 139 **Array with subType:** 140 ```json 141 { 142 "id": "emailList", 143 "direction": "in", 144 "type": "array", 145 "subType": "string", 146 "defaultValue": ["admin@example.com"] 147 } 148 ``` 149 150 **Input associated with a trigger:** 151 ```json 152 { 153 "id": "webhookPayload", 154 "direction": "in", 155 "type": "object", 156 "triggerNodeId": "start" 157 } 158 ``` 159 Accessed in expressions as `$vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id}` (the variable is nested under the trigger node's output — NOT `$vars.{id}`). 160 161 162 **File input (`type: "file"`):** 163 ```json 164 { 165 "id": "inputDoc", 166 "direction": "in", 167 "type": "file", 168 "description": "Document uploaded at trigger / bound via --attachment", 169 "triggerNodeId": "start" 170 } 171 ``` 172 173 > **Runtime shape of a `file` variable.** At runtime a `file` variable is an **object** (the *Flow Attachment* object), not a string. A Script node reading `$vars.start.output.inputDoc` receives: 174 > 175 > ```json 176 > { "ID": "", "FullName": "report.pdf", "MimeType": "application/pdf", "Metadata": { "size": "1024" } } 177 > ``` 178 > 179 > The uploaded file's name is **`.FullName`**. Property access is **case-sensitive** at runtime — these exact casings resolve, others return `undefined`/`null`: `.ID` (uppercase, not `.Id`), `.FullName`, `.MimeType`, and the **nested `.Metadata.size`** (lowercase `size`, NOT `.Size`). `.name` / `.fileName` do **not** exist. Two layers: the `.flow` *declaration* is camelCase (`type`, `direction`); the *runtime* object carries the casing above. Do NOT write `"FullName"` into the `.flow` source. Bind the file with `uip maestro flow debug --attachment =` — see [cli-commands.md — Pre-flight](cli-commands.md#attachment-preflight). 180 181 ### Type Reference 182 183 | Type | Default Value | Notes | 184 | --- | --- | --- | 185 | `string` | `""` | Default type if omitted | 186 | `number` | `0` | Integer or float | 187 | `boolean` | `false` | | 188 | `object` | `{}` | Use `schema` for structured objects | 189 | `array` | `[]` | Use `subType` for typed arrays | 190 | `file` | — | Bound at runtime via `--attachment`; hydrates as an object — read `.FullName` (see [File input](#file-input) above) | 191 192 --- 193 194 ## Node Variables (`nodes`) 195 196 Node variables represent outputs produced by nodes during execution. They are read-only and referenced via `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}`. 197 198 When you add a node via `uip maestro flow node add`, node variables are created automatically. When using `Edit` against the `.flow` file, add them manually. 199 200 ### Schema 201 202 ```typescript 203 { 204 id: string // Format: "{nodeId}.{outputId}" 205 type?: string // Output type 206 subType?: string // For complex types 207 schema?: object // JSON Schema for structured outputs 208 description?: string // What this output contains 209 binding: { 210 nodeId: string // Source node ID 211 outputId: string // Output port ID (e.g., "output", "error") 212 } 213 } 214 ``` 215 216 ### Example 217 218 ```json 219 { 220 "variables": { 221 "nodes": [ 222 { 223 "id": "fetchData.output", 224 "type": "object", 225 "description": "HTTP response body", 226 "binding": { 227 "nodeId": "fetchData", 228 "outputId": "output" 229 } 230 }, 231 { 232 "id": "fetchData.error", 233 "type": "object", 234 "description": "Error details if the request fails", 235 "schema": { 236 "$schema": "http://json-schema.org/draft-07/schema#", 237 "type": "object", 238 "required": ["code", "message"], 239 "properties": { 240 "code": { "type": "string" }, 241 "message": { "type": "string" }, 242 "detail": { "type": "string" }, 243 "category": { "type": "string" }, 244 "status": { "type": "integer" } 245 } 246 }, 247 "binding": { 248 "nodeId": "fetchData", 249 "outputId": "error" 250 } 251 } 252 ] 253 } 254 } 255 ``` 256 257 --- 258 259 ## Variable Updates (`variableUpdates`) 260 261 Variable updates assign new values to `inout` (state) variables at specific nodes. They execute when the node completes. 262 263 ### Schema 264 265 ```typescript 266 { 267 "variableUpdates": { 268 "{nodeId}": [ 269 { 270 "variableId": string, // ID of the inout variable to update 271 "expression": string // =js: expression to evaluate and assign 272 } 273 ] 274 } 275 } 276 ``` 277 278 ### Example 279 280 ```json 281 { 282 "variables": { 283 "globals": [ 284 { 285 "id": "counter", 286 "direction": "inout", 287 "type": "number", 288 "defaultValue": 0 289 }, 290 { 291 "id": "lastStatus", 292 "direction": "inout", 293 "type": "string", 294 "defaultValue": "pending" 295 } 296 ], 297 "variableUpdates": { 298 "processItem": [ 299 { 300 "variableId": "counter", 301 "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" 302 }, 303 { 304 "variableId": "lastStatus", 305 "expression": "=js:$vars.processItem.output.status" 306 } 307 ] 308 } 309 } 310 } 311 ``` 312 313 > **Only `inout` variables can be updated.** Updating an `in` or `out` variable is invalid. 314 315 > **Inside loops:** variableUpdate expressions cannot access loop iteration variables like `$vars..currentItem`. Those are only available inside the body node's script. The variableUpdate must reference the body node's output (e.g., `=js:$vars.bodyNode.output`). 316 317 --- 318 319 ## Output Mapping on End Nodes 320 321 Workflow output variables (`direction: "out"`) must be mapped on End nodes. The End node's `outputs` object maps each output variable ID to a source expression. 322 323 ### Structure 324 325 ```json 326 { 327 "id": "end1", 328 "type": "core.control.end", 329 "typeVersion": "1.0", 330 "display": { "label": "End" }, 331 "inputs": {}, 332 "outputs": { 333 "totalAmount": { 334 "source": "=js:$vars.calculateTotal.output.amount" 335 }, 336 "summary": { 337 "source": "=js:$vars.formatResult.output.text" 338 } 339 } 340 } 341 ``` 342 343 > **Every `out` variable must have a mapping on every End node** that the flow can reach. Missing mappings cause runtime errors. 344 345 --- 346 347 ## Expression System 348 349 Flow uses a **Jint-based JavaScript engine** (ES2020 subset) for expressions. There are two expression formats. 350 351 ### `=js:` Expressions (Full JavaScript) 352 353 Used for conditions, input values, variable updates, and output mappings. The `=js:` prefix tells the engine to evaluate the rest as JavaScript. 354 355 ``` 356 =js:$vars.order.amount > 1000 && $vars.order.status === "approved" 357 ``` 358 359 ### Template Expressions (`{ }`) 360 361 Used for string interpolation in **native flow string fields** only. Expressions inside single braces are evaluated and converted to strings. 362 363 ``` 364 Order {$vars.orderId} is {$vars.status} — total: {$vars.amount} 365 ``` 366 367 > **Brace-templates do NOT work in Integration Service activity inputs.** The flow-layer template runner only processes native flow fields (decision expressions, variable updates, end-node output `source`, script bodies, agent prompt text). Fields inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters` on `core.action.http.v2` or `uipath.connector.*` activity nodes — `url`, `headers`, `body`, `query` — are passed through to the IS runtime unchanged, so `{$vars.article}` ships literally. Observed behavior: the `$` is stripped and the braces survive (`user/{vars.article}` reaches the service). **For any dynamic value in an IS activity input, use `=js:` instead** — e.g., `` "url": "=js:`https://.../user/${$vars.article}`" `` or `"headers": { "Authorization": "=js:'Bearer ' + $vars.token" }`. 368 369 ### IS Activity Inputs Require `=js:` (Critical) 370 371 Every `$vars` / `$metadata` / `$self` reference inside `inputs.detail.bodyParameters`, `inputs.detail.queryParameters`, or `inputs.detail.pathParameters` on a connector or HTTP activity node MUST be wrapped with `=js:`. Without it the value ships as a literal string at runtime. 372 373 | Wrong | Right | 374 |---|---| 375 | `"recordId": "$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 376 | `"recordId": "nodes.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 377 | `"recordId": "{vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id}"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 378 | `"recordId": "=js:createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | `"recordId": "=js:$vars.createEntityRecord1.output.Id"` | 379 380 The serializer rewrites `$vars` → `vars` whether or not `=js:` is present, so a missing prefix yields a confusing failure: the runtime field is bound to the literal string `"vars.X.output.Id"` (which looks like an unevaluated expression). The last row above is the opposite mistake — `=js:` is present but the `$vars.` prefix on the node reference is missing, so the expression evaluates a bare (undefined) identifier instead of the node's output. `flow validate` catches this (cli-side `expression-prefix-validator`, error with remediation hint) — older cli versions without the validator still let it through to `flow debug`. See [node-output-wiring.md](node-output-wiring.md) for the full per-node-type field reference (MST-9107). 381 382 ### Comparison 383 384 | Feature | `=js:` | `{ }` template | 385 | --- | --- | --- | 386 | Return type | Any (boolean, number, object, array) | Always string | 387 | Use case | Conditions, inputs, mappings | Native flow text/prompt fields only | 388 | Works in IS activity inputs (HTTP URL/headers/body, connector `bodyParameters`) | Yes | **No — use `=js:`** | 389 | Full JS | Yes | Expression-only (no statements) | 390 | Prefix | `=js:` required | No prefix, braces inline | 391 392 --- 393 394 ## Available Globals 395 396 These variables are available in all expression contexts: 397 398 | Global | Description | Access pattern | 399 | --- | --- | --- | 400 | `$vars` | All workflow and node variables | `$vars.{variableId}` or `$vars.{nodeId}.{outputId}` | 401 | `$metadata` | Workflow metadata (instanceId, executionId) | `$metadata.instanceId` | 402 | `$self` | Current node's output (HTTP branch conditions only) | `$self.output.statusCode` | 403 | `$vars..*` | Loop iteration context (inside loops only) | `$vars.loop1.currentItem`, `$vars.loop1.currentIndex` | 404 405 ### `$vars` Access Patterns 406 407 ```javascript 408 // Workflow global 409 $vars.customerName 410 $vars.counter 411 412 // Trigger-associated flow input (triggerNodeId set) 413 $vars.{triggerNodeId}.output.{id} 414 415 // File input (type: "file") → object, read .FullName for the name 416 $vars.start.output.inputDoc.FullName 417 418 // Node output (script node) 419 $vars.script1.output 420 $vars.script1.output.someField 421 422 // Node output (HTTP node) 423 $vars.fetchData.output.body 424 $vars.fetchData.output.statusCode 425 $vars.fetchData.output.headers 426 427 // Node error 428 $vars.fetchData.error.message 429 $vars.fetchData.error.code 430 ``` 431 432 --- 433 434 ## 8	
9	A frequent request: *"Can my existing project — e.g. a low-code agent plus a coded (C#) RPA rule engine — become a Maestro flow, and what would the structure look like?"*
10	
11	There is **no automatic "turn this project into a flow" conversion, and you shouldn't want one.** You don't rewrite the project into a flow — you **re-host the orchestration and keep the parts**:
12	
13	1. **Keep the executors as-is.** Existing coded/RPA components and any existing agent stay their own artifacts. They are **not** rewritten into Maestro — they become **resource nodes** the flow calls (`uipath.core.rpa-workflow.*`, `uipath.core.agent.*`). See the relevant plugin's `planning.md`.
14	2. **Lift only the orchestration into Maestro.** The control flow currently implicit in the rule engine (what runs first, what waits, what branches) becomes the explicit flow topology — trigger → steps → decisions → end.
15	3. **Make every wait a first-class node.** Anything the old code did with sleeps, polling loops, or "check again later" becomes a Maestro wait/delay/HITL/`create-and-wait` node — that visibility is the whole reason to move.
16	4. **Publish (or keep in-solution), then reference.** Each executor is published or kept as a sibling project so the flow's registry resolves it (`registry list --local` for in-solution).

**Generic activity, retrieve-by-id** (Salesforce `get-record` against Account — object plus a path parameter for the record ID):

```bash
uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> \
  --detail '{"connectionId": "<id>", "folderKey": "<key>", "method": "GETBYID", "endpoint": "/Account/{accountId}", "objectName": "Account", "pathParameters": {"accountId": "001KY000007uI02YAE"}}' \
  --output json
```

Path-parameterized GETs are a distinct shape from list/query: `endpoint` carries `{<placeholder>}` tokens and `pathParameters` supplies the values. Resolve the ID via `is resources run list <connector-key> <objectName>` (Step 4) — never paste IDs across connections (see [reference-resolution.md](../../../../../../uipath-platform/references/integration-service/reference-resolution.md#reference-ids-are-connection-scoped-critical)).

The `objectName` field is required for generic nodes (see "Generic vs Concrete Activities" above). The CLI fails fast with a runnable hint when it's missing on a generic node. For concrete nodes the field is ignored if supplied.

**Source of truth for `method` and `endpoint`** — pick either (both read the same upstream IS metadata):

- `registry get` (Step 2) → `connectorMethodInfo.method` and `connectorMethodInfo.path` — populated for **concrete** activities only.
- `is resources describe <connector-key> <objectName> --operation <Op>` (Step 3) → `availableOperations[].method` and `availableOperations[].path` — works for both, and is the only source for **generic** activities.

> **Method label — pass the IS describe value verbatim.** `is resources describe` sometimes returns synthesized IS-side labels (notably `"GETBYID"` for path-parameterized retrieve operations). The CLI accepts both standard HTTP verbs (`GET`, `POST`, …) and IS-side labels (`GETBYID`) — copy `operation.method` from `is resources describe` as-is and the CLI normalizes to the underlying HTTP verb internally. Don't translate by hand.

> **`flow validate` cross-checks `method` against the activity's `operation`.** If the value you pass disagrees with the operation baked into the node by `node add` (e.g. `method: "POST"` on a Retrieve activity), validate fails with `HTTP method "<X>" does not match operation "<Y>". Expected "<Z>"`. This catches stale copy-paste — fix by re-reading `operation.method` from `is resources describe` against the right `--operation`.

Body field names in `bodyParameters` come from `inputDefinition.fields[].name` (`registry get`, concrete only) or `requestFields[].name` (`is resources describe`, both).

> **Array fields — `[*]` indicates an array.** `[*]` in `requestFields[].name` (or `inputDefinition.fields[].name`) marks the field as an array; `dataType` identifies the element type. **Supported only when `[*]` is the name suffix.** Any name containing `[*].` (path segments after the `[*]`, e.g. `addresses[*].zipCode`, `contacts[*].emails[*]`) is not authorable — the canvas UI does not emit these shapes. The rule below covers `bodyParameters`, `queryParameters`, and `pathParameters`.
>
> | `requestFields[].name` | `dataType` | Authoring shape in `inputs.detail` |
> |---|---|---|
> | `fields.labels[*]` | `string` | `"fields.labels": "=js:(['shield', 'p0'])"` |
> | `fields.components_arrayRemap_name[*]` | `string` | `"fields.components_arrayRemap_name": "=js:(['IS Runtime'])"` |
> | `users[*]` | `string` | `"users": "=js:(['U123ABC', 'U456DEF'])"` |
>
> **Strip `[*]` from the key; pass a `=js:` expression returning the array.**  The runtime rejects any key containing the literal `[*]` substring as unknown (regardless of value shape), so pass the stripped form in your `node configure --detail` payload. **A literal JSON array (`"users": ["U123ABC", "U456DEF"]`) passes `node configure` and `flow validate` but does not bind — the field round-trips empty.** **Distinct from `customFieldsRequestDetails.parameterValues`**, where `[*]` is encoded as `_array` — see Step 6c.
>
> **Expression values.** The serializer is purely structural (dot-expansion only; no expression evaluation, no type coercion). Choose the authoring shape based on what the expression returns at runtime:
>
> | Expression resolves to | Authoring shape | Example |
> |---|---|---|
> | The whole array | `"<field>": "=<expr>"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:$vars.allTags"` |
> | A single element to wrap | `"<field>": "=js:([<expr>])"` | `"fields.labels": "=js:([$vars.priorityTag])"` |

> **Connector output shape — derive it from `connectorMethodInfo`, never from vendor-API intuition.**
>
> | `connectorMethodInfo.operation` | `output` at runtime | Loop / binding shape |
> |---|---|---|
> | `list` | bare **array**; `outputResponseDefinition.fields` describes one element | `"collection": "=js:$vars.<node>.output"` |
> | anything else (`retrieve`, `create`, `update`, …) | single **object** matching those fields | `=js:$vars.<node>.output.<field>` |
>
> Ignore `outputDefinition.output.type` — it says `"object"` even for `list` operations, where the actual output type is an array.

The command populates `inputs.detail` and creates workflow-level `bindings` entries. Use **resolved IDs** from Step 4, not display names. For FilterBuilder params, see Step 6a.

When inspecting the resulting `.flow`, note that the folder field is named `connectionFolderKey` in `inputs.detail`. The CLI `--detail` input accepts `folderKey` for convenience, then serializes the `.flow` field expected by validation. Do not hand-edit this field — `inputs.detail` is CLI-owned (see [Author capability — Node ownership](../../../CAPABILITY.md#node-ownership--who-authors-the-node)); re-run `node configure` to change it.

> **Do not use `filterExpression`** — that field is the trigger / JMESPath path. See [connector-trigger/impl.md](../connector-trigger/impl.md#filter-trees).

> **Shell quoting tip:** For complex `--detail` JSON, write it to a temp file: `uip maestro flow node configure <file> <nodeId> --detail "$(cat /tmp/detail.json)" --output json`

#### Step 6c — Populate custom fields (api-type ObjectActions)

A connector activity has a **parent-field-driven schema** when its valid input fields are not fixed in static metadata but are computed at design time by running an api-type ObjectAction against the IS Element Service. Examples: Jira's `Create Issue` schema depends on the project + issue type; Snowflake's `executeQuery` response columns depend on the SQL string; Dataservice V3's entity field set depends on `tenantEntityName`. The activity persists the parent-field values in `essentialConfiguration.customFieldsRequestDetails` so the runtime can replay the schema-fetch ObjectAction on each invocation. The CLI passes this through verbatim.

**How DAP determines support — check both metadata locations.** An api-type action may live at either:

- Top-level `objectActions[]` with PascalCase `ActionType: "Api"` (older shape, e.g. Jira `GenerateSchema`)
- `connectorMethodInfo.design.actions[]` with lowercase `actionType: "api"` (newer shape, e.g. Dataservice V3 `FetchObjectMetadataTenant`)

Always inspect both locations from `registry get` output before deciding the connector has none.

The matching action is then selected by one of two rule sources:

- **`source: field`** — the action's `rules[].refFieldName` are satisfied by user-supplied `-f, --field` values (typically SQL-style query connectors where the query string is the parent field).
- **`source: method`** — the action is declared at the operation level and matched against the operation's HTTP method (typically CRUD activities).

Based on a thorough search of the entire skill directory, here is what I found — and did not find.

## What I found

The `.flow` file format has a schema-versioned migration chain, documented only in one place:

**`/home/azureuser/projects/skills/skills/uipath-maestro-flow/references/author/references/brownfield.md`, lines 59–67** ("Refusing to serialize a vX workflow" — migrate first):

> `migrate` is lossless — it walks the per-version migration chain (e.g. `=js:` expression strings become rich expression objects) and bumps the file to the current version.

This is the only place in the skill docs that hints at what changes across a migration step, and it names a `migrate` command:

```bash
uip maestro flow migrate <ProjectName>.flow --output json
```

That one line — "`=js:` expression strings become rich expression objects" — is directly relevant to your error, since `variableUpdates.multiplyItem.0.expression` is currently authored as an `=js:`-prefixed string. It strongly suggests the 1.9→1.10 step is exactly this transformation: converting the plain string `"expression": "=js:...` into some structured/object form (a "rich expression object") rather than a bare string. But the docs do **not** spell out the object's exact shape (no `kind`/`value`/`type` field names are given anywhere in the skill).

## What I did NOT find

- No file in the skill (`references/diagnose/failure-modes.md`, `references/diagnose/troubleshooting-guide.md`, `references/shared/file-format.md`, `references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md`, `references/shared/cli-commands.md`, `references/shared/cli-conventions.md`, or any `author/references/plugins/*` doc) mentions "1.9" or "1.10" as version numbers, or documents a `variableUpdates[].expression` shape other than the plain string form:
  ```json
  { "variableId": "counter", "expression": "=js:$vars.counter + 1" }
  ```
  (from `references/shared/variables-and-expressions.md`, lines 267–275 and 297–307 — this is the exact pattern you used, and it's the only shape documented anywhere in the skill).
- No JSON example anywhere shows a "rich expression object" — no `value`, `kind`, `type`, or wrapper-object shape is given for `expression` fields in `variableUpdates`.
- No migration changelog, versioned schema spec, or MST/DNA ticket in `failure-modes.md` covers this specific migration step (the tickets that do exist — MST-9107, MST-9972, MST-9061 — are about expression prefixes, `variables.nodes[]` regeneration, and layout rendering, not this migration).

## Conclusion and recommendation

The skill docs confirm this is a real, expected migration step (string expressions → "rich expression objects" per brownfield.md) but do not give the target JSON shape for `variableUpdates[].expression`. Rather than guess the shape (`value` vs. wrapping object vs. additional field), I'd recommend:

If you want to see the shape without touching your file, **scaffold a throwaway flow** with a loop/accumulator pattern via `uip maestro flow init` (or `node add`/`node configure` for a loop node) and inspect its `variableUpdates` JSON directly — per `file-format.md` line 44's convention: "To see the current value, scaffold a throwaway flow with `init` and read its top-level `version`, or read it from an existing `init`-generated `.flow`."
